title: The Last Flight
vision: The plane rolls onto the runway.
wake: You open your eyes. You’re on the plane, seat 14C. Tomorrow is the job interview of your life, and the plane is just getting ready for take-off.

cabin.text: The engines are starting. You just saw this plane burn at the end of the runway. Next to you, Daniel is biting his nails.

left.label: Stand up, warn everyone
left.past: You warned everyone on the plane
left.after: People shout at you. The crew takes you off the plane. Daniel follows you: “I’m not flying either.”

right.label: Say you feel sick, get off quietly
right.past: You got off the plane without telling anyone
right.after: A flight attendant walks you to the door. Behind you, nobody moves.

jetbridge.text: You run up the jet bridge. Your shoelace comes undone and drags on the floor.

left.label: Stop and tie it
left.past: You tied your shoelace
left.after: You’re the last one off. Behind you, the plane door closes.

right.label: Keep running
right.past: You kept running with your shoelace undone
right.after: You reach the terminal. The lace is still dragging on the floor.

window.text: The plane takes off. At the end of the runway, a flash, then fire. Everyone runs to the window.

left.label: Film it on your phone
left.past: You filmed the burning plane and the video spread
left.after: You film all of it. An hour later the video is everywhere, and so is your face.

right.label: Turn away
right.past: You didn’t look at the burning plane
right.after: You only hear the explosion. That is bad enough.

escalator.text: Everyone is going down to arrivals. The escalator is packed, and people are coming up the stairs next to it.

left.label: Take the escalator
left.past: You took the crowded escalator
left.after: The steps carry you down slowly. Downstairs, the queues are starting.

right.label: Take the stairs
right.past: You took the stairs against the crowd and fell behind
right.after: You go down slowly against the crowd. Downstairs, the queues are already long.

police.text: Two officers take you into a room. “How did you know the plane would burn?”

left.label: Tell him about the vision
left.past: You told the police about the vision
left.after: He doesn’t believe you, but it feels good to say it. They keep you three hours in a room with no windows and give you a sandwich.

right.label: “I had a panic attack”
right.past: You lied to the police
right.after: Novak looks you in the eye for a long time. He writes your name in his notebook and lets you go.

variants: Two officers take you into a room. Your video is playing on a phone on the table. “How did you know the plane would burn?”
Two officers take you into a room. “You told everyone on the plane it would burn. How did you know?”

cafe.text: Your hands are shaking. The same pictures are on the TV again. The waiter: “What can I get you?”

left.label: A proper breakfast
left.past: You had breakfast at the airport
left.after: Eggs, bread, hot tea. Your legs feel stronger.

right.label: A double espresso
right.past: You drank a double espresso
right.after: Your head clears. For a while, your hands stop shaking.

recruiter.text: The company you were flying to calls. “Was that your plane? Oh my God. Can we do the interview online tonight at 21:00?”

left.label: “Yes, tonight”
left.past: You agreed to an online interview tonight
left.after: After the call you remember: you have your laptop, but the charger was in your suitcase. And the suitcase was on the plane.

right.label: “I can’t do it today”
right.past: You cancelled the job interview
right.after: “I understand,” she says. Something changes in her voice. The job is gone.

variants: Your phone rings in the police room and the officer lets you answer. It’s the company you were flying to: “Was that your plane? Can we do the interview online tonight at 21:00?”

airline.text: “Your bag was on the plane, we’re so sorry. You get a room at the airport hotel and a seat on tomorrow’s 06:00 flight.” The hotel shuttle leaves in an hour. By the door, a man whispers: “Need a taxi?”

left.label: Wait for the shuttle
left.past: You waited for the hotel shuttle
left.after: You wait an hour in the crowd. The shuttle drops you at the hotel door.

right.label: Take his taxi
right.past: You got into an unlicensed taxi with a broken seatbelt
right.after: There’s no taxi sign on the car. In the back seat, the seatbelt buckle is broken.

variants: “Your bag was on the plane, we’re so sorry. You get a room at the airport hotel and a seat on tomorrow’s 06:00 flight.” The shuttle just left, the next one is in an hour. By the door, a man whispers: “Need a taxi?”

ride.text: The driver goes very fast and keeps looking at you in the mirror. “I know you from somewhere.” A fire truck is coming the other way on the narrow road.

left.label: “Watch the road!”
left.past: You shouted at the driver
left.after: He brakes hard and you hit the seat in front. Angry, he drops you in the rain a kilometre before the hotel.

right.label: Chat with him
right.past: You chatted with the unlicensed driver
right.after: You talk about football. He can’t place your face. The fire truck rushes past you.

reception.text: “We have two rooms left. One on the ninth floor with a balcony, but the fire-stairs door doesn’t close properly. Or one on the ground floor, next to the boiler room. It gets a bit warm.”

left.label: The ninth floor
left.past: You took the room on the ninth floor
left.after: From the balcony you can see the runway. Planes take off, again and again.

right.label: The ground floor
right.past: You took the room next to the boiler room
right.after: The room is warm. A deep hum comes from behind the wall.

variants: Daniel arrives too, with the same voucher. Reception: “We have two rooms left. One on the ninth floor with a balcony, but the fire-stairs door doesn’t close properly. Or one on the ground floor, next to the boiler room. It gets a bit warm.” Daniel will take the other one.

charger.text: “A charger? This is all we have, five euros.” No brand, a thin cable. The nearest electronics shop is a twenty-five-minute walk in the rain.

left.label: Buy the five-euro one
left.past: You bought a cheap no-name charger at reception
left.after: It buzzes a little when you plug it in. The laptop is charging, and that’s what matters.

right.label: Walk to the shop in the rain
right.past: You walked in the rain for a proper charger
right.after: Fifty minutes later you’re back, soaked, with a proper charger in a box.

sister.text: Fourteen missed calls. Then a message: “Your name is on the passenger list! Please pick up!”

left.label: Call her, say you’re alive
left.past: You called your sister and told her you’re alive
left.after: You both cry. When you hang up, your shoulders feel lighter.

right.label: Just text: “I’m fine”
right.past: You only texted your sister and didn’t call
right.after: “I need to hear your voice,” she writes. You don’t answer.

rest.text: All your strength is gone. But when you close your eyes, you see the fire again.

left.label: Sleep a little
left.past: You slept in the afternoon
left.after: Two hours of nightmares. You wake up with a rested body, but not a rested mind.

right.label: Walk around the hotel
right.past: You walked around and found the second staircase
right.after: At the far end of the corridor you find a second staircase. The door says “Staff only”, but it isn’t locked.

window-high.text: The room is hot and stuffy. The window opens all the way. A plane takes off every four minutes and the glass shakes.

left.label: Open it wide
left.past: You left the ninth-floor window wide open
left.after: Cool air hits your face. The draught slams the room door shut.

right.label: Keep it shut
right.past: You kept the window shut
right.after: It’s hot but quiet. You only see the planes now.

spa.text: Reception added a spa pass to your voucher. The rain has stopped and the garden is empty.

left.label: The hot pool at the spa
left.past: You went into the hot pool at the spa
left.after: Your muscles relax. Your head feels a little heavy.

right.label: Walk in the garden
right.past: You saw smoke coming from the boiler room
right.after: The fresh air helps. Smoke comes out of a basement window by the boiler room, and it smells like gas.

news.text: “Six passengers left the plane before take-off. One of them acted as if they knew everything in advance.”

left.label: Watch until the end
left.past: You watched the news until the end
left.after: A crack in a fuel line. The photos of the dead appear one by one.

right.label: Turn it off
right.past: You turned off the news
right.after: The room goes quiet. Not knowing is better, for now.

variants: “Only one passenger left the plane before take-off.” Your face is on the screen. Next to it, the photos of the dead: 14B, Daniel.

dinner.text: You haven’t had a real meal all day.

left.label: Room service
left.past: You ate in your room
left.after: The waiter puts down the tray and mutters: “The boiler’s broken again, the water’s only warm.” The food is good, but you’re alone, and the TV is on the news again.

right.label: The hotel restaurant
right.past: You ate in the restaurant
right.after: You warm up. A faint smell of gas comes from behind the kitchen, but the waiters don’t seem to care.

smell.text: There is a heavy smell of gas in the corridor. A deep hum is coming from somewhere.

left.label: Tell reception
left.past: You reported the smell of gas
left.after: “It’s an old boiler, it’s normal,” they say. But someone calls the basement on the radio, and they go to check the ground-floor rooms.

right.label: It’s an old hotel, forget it
right.past: You told no one about the gas
right.after: You go back to your room. The smell stays with you for a while.

variants: There is a heavy smell of gas in the corridor. You think of the smoking basement window in the garden.

bar.text: The barman is wiping glasses. “Long day?”

left.label: One drink, for your nerves
left.past: You drank at the bar in the evening
left.after: Warmth spreads through your chest. Another glass arrives.

right.label: Drink water
right.past: You only drank water at the bar
right.after: Cold water. Your head stays clear.

variants: Daniel is at the bar with his third glass. “Sit down. If we don’t drink today, when will we?”

rooftop.text: Daniel is by the rooftop pool, drunk, sitting on the glass railing. His feet are swinging over the drop.

left.label: Run and pull him back
left.past: You ran to pull Daniel off the railing
left.after: You grab his arm and pull. You both fall on the wet floor. Daniel laughs, then cries.

right.label: Call reception
right.past: You called reception instead of pulling Daniel back
right.after: When the staff get there, the railing is empty.

roof-alone.text: There’s nobody on the roof. One panel of the glass railing is loose and rattles in the wind. The runway is all lights.

left.label: Watch the runway from the glass
left.past: You leaned on the loose glass railing to watch the runway
left.after: A plane takes off. Your eyes burn, but you keep watching.

right.label: Sit on a sun lounger
right.past: You sat on a lounger on the roof
right.after: Planes pass over your head. You start counting them.

interview.text: Three faces on the screen. “Can you tell us about a time you made a quick decision under pressure?”

left.label: Tell them you got off the plane
left.past: You told the interviewers about getting off the plane
left.after: A silence. Then Ms Lang smiles: “I don’t think there’s a better example.”

right.label: Give a textbook answer
right.past: You gave a textbook answer in the interview
right.after: They politely take notes. Nobody smiles.

hotplug.text: The interview is over. The charger is very hot and smells of plastic. The laptop battery is still at 5%.

left.label: Leave it charging overnight
left.past: You left the hot charger plugged in for the night
left.after: You leave the plug alone. Its buzz mixes with the silence of the room.

right.label: Unplug it
right.past: You unplugged the charger
right.after: The plastic burns your fingers. The laptop goes dark.

novak.text: Inspector Novak is at the door. “A panic attack, was it? There’s no panic attack in your records. Let’s talk.”

left.label: Let him in, tell him everything
left.past: You told Novak everything and he stayed in your room
left.after: He doesn’t believe you. But he stays, listens and takes notes. An hour goes by.

right.label: Don’t open
right.past: You didn’t open the door to Novak
right.after: He knocks for a while. Then his steps go away.

bath.text: You need something to calm down. The bath is big. Your phone is at 8%.

left.label: A hot bath, phone charging on the edge
left.past: You took a bath with your phone charging on the edge
left.after: The hot water washes the whole day away. Your eyes are almost closing.

right.label: A quick shower
right.past: You took a quick shower
right.after: Five minutes. The phone stays in the room.

sleep.text: Your eyes are closing. The bed has never looked so soft.

left.label: Lie down
left.past: You lay down and fell asleep
left.after: You fall asleep. After a while, you smell something.

right.label: Stay up
right.past: You stayed up instead of sleeping
right.after: You watch the planes from the window. Your legs feel heavy.

alarm.text: The alarm goes off. Smoke is coming under the door. A bang from downstairs.

left.label: Run into the corridor
left.past: You ran into the corridor during the fire
left.after: The corridor is full of smoke. You keep low and move on.

right.label: Stay, wet towels under the door
right.past: You stayed in your room during the fire
right.after: You push the towels under the door. Minutes later, a fire ladder appears at the window.
variants: You push the towels under the door. Minutes later, a firefighter breaks your window and pulls you out.
The alarm goes off. Novak jumps up: “I’ve done a fire drill in this hotel. Follow me and do what I say.”

stairs-fire.text: Someone is lying on the stairs in the smoke: the receptionist. She has twisted her ankle and reaches out when she sees you.

left.label: Lift her up, go down together
left.past: You carried the fallen receptionist down the smoky stairs
left.after: You put her arm over your shoulder. Every step takes a minute.

right.label: Step over her and go
right.past: You left the receptionist on the stairs
right.after: Behind you, someone whose name you don’t know calls out to you. You don’t turn back.

exit-door.text: The lobby is full of smoke. The main door is swollen from the heat and stuck. To the right, the kitchen door is open; there should be another exit behind it.

left.label: Push the door with your shoulder
left.past: You forced the stuck door with your shoulder
left.after: One, two… on the third try the door opens and you fall into the rain.

right.label: Go round through the kitchen
right.past: You went through the kitchen next to the boiler room
right.after: You go through the kitchen and out of the back door into the garden.

variants: The lobby is full of smoke. The main door is swollen from the heat and stuck. The receptionist grabs your arm: “Not through the kitchen! The boiler is there!”

count.text: Everyone is counted in the rain, under blankets. A cleaner from the fourth floor is missing. The firefighters are looking for another way in.

left.label: Go back in with the firefighters
left.past: You went back into the burning hotel with the firefighters
left.after: You show them the second staircase. In the smoke you find a voice first, then a hand. When you come out, the firefighters pat you on the back.

right.label: Tell the firefighters and wait
right.past: You waited outside
right.after: You watch the door. The minutes don’t move.

variants: Everyone is counted in the rain, under blankets. Daniel isn’t there. The firefighters are looking for another way in.
Everyone is counted in the rain, under blankets. The receptionist you left on the stairs isn’t there. The firefighters are looking for another way in.

boarding.text: An airline agent hands out blankets and boarding passes. “Tomorrow, the 06:00 flight. Same seat: 14C.”

left.label: Take the boarding pass
left.past: You took the boarding pass for the 06:00 flight
left.after: The pass gets wet in your hand. 14C.

right.label: “I’ll never fly again”
right.past: You tore up the boarding pass
right.after: You tear the pass in two. The agent shrugs and moves on.

escalator.title: The Escalator
escalator.text: Your eyes were on the video on your phone. Your loose lace got caught in the teeth of the step and pulled you down.
escalator.hint: Tying a shoe takes ten seconds.

windscreen.title: The Windscreen
windscreen.text: “Ha! You’re the guy from the video!” The driver turned round. The fire truck was right there on the narrow road, and there was no belt in the back.

rooftop.title: The Roof
rooftop.text: You pulled Daniel back and he fell to the floor. With the drinks in you, you lost your balance and went over the railing.
rooftop.omen: The world is spinning a little.

roofAlone.title: The Glass Railing
roofAlone.text: The drinks from the bar made you dizzy. The loose glass panel couldn’t hold your weight.
roofAlone.hint: The rattling glass was trying to tell you something.

bath.title: The Bath
bath.text: The five-euro charger touched the water. You were in the bath.
bath.hint: You pay for cheap things later.

ringing.title: The Ringing Phone
ringing.text: Your sister kept calling because she never heard your voice. You reached for the charging phone with a wet hand.
ringing.hint: One phone call would have been enough.

drown.title: Asleep in the Bath
drown.text: The drinks and the hot water put you to sleep. The water slowly rose.

chargerfire.title: The Charger
chargerfire.text: The five-euro charger got hotter all night. While you slept, the first spark fell on the carpet.
chargerfire.hint: The smell of plastic was a warning.

smoke.title: Smoke
smoke.text: The fire-stairs door didn’t close, and smoke filled the stairs up to the ninth floor. You didn’t know another way down.
smoke.hint: Reception told you about that door.
smoke.omen: Smoke is rising up the stairs.

draft.title: The Open Window
draft.text: The window was wide open. The draught pulled the smoke into the room under the wet towels.
draft.hint: You should have known when the door slammed.

boiler.title: The Boiler Room
boiler.text: The fire was on the other side of your wall. Nobody had checked the boiler, and nobody knocked on your door.
boiler.hint: Reporting the smell would have taken a minute.

stairsFall.title: The Fire Stairs
stairsFall.text: The drinks had made your legs weak. You and the receptionist fell down the stairs together.

kitchenFire.title: The Kitchen
kitchenFire.text: The boiler was right behind the kitchen. Nobody had reported the gas, and there was no one with you to say “Not that way.”
kitchenFire.hint: The receptionist you left on the stairs knew the way.
kitchenFire.omen: A hiss is coming from the kitchen.

backIn.title: Going Back
backIn.text: In the smoke you lost the firefighters. You didn’t know the inside of the hotel.
backIn.hint: You could have walked around the hotel that afternoon.

panic-work.title: The Terminal
panic-work.text: You couldn’t breathe and started to run. A luggage trolley knocked you down.
panic-work.hint: You ran from the plane, but not from yourself.
panic-work.omen: Your heart is beating very fast.

panic-street.title: In the Rain
panic-street.text: You couldn’t breathe and ran into the road. You saw the lights too late.
panic-street.hint: Sometimes the biggest danger is in your own head.
panic-street.omen: Your heart is beating very fast.

panic-home.title: The Hotel Stairs
panic-home.text: You couldn’t breathe and ran for the hotel stairs. You missed a step.
panic-home.hint: The day didn’t lose you. You lost the day.
panic-home.omen: Your heart is beating very fast.

collapse-work.title: The Baggage Belt
collapse-work.text: You felt dizzy and fell against the edge of the baggage belt.
collapse-work.hint: Your body gives up at some point too.

collapse-street.title: The Pavement
collapse-street.text: You felt dizzy and fell on the edge of the wet pavement.
collapse-street.hint: Your body gives up at some point too.

collapse-home.title: The Bathroom Floor
collapse-home.text: You felt dizzy and fell on the bathroom tiles.
collapse-home.hint: Your body gives up at some point too.

two.title: Two of Us
two.text: 00:00. Daniel is next to you, shaking under a blanket. You saved him twice.
two.hint: Today, death went home empty-handed twice.

one-more.title: One More
one-more.text: 00:00. The person you brought out of the smoke is in the ambulance, breathing. So are you.
one-more.hint: Today, one name came off the list.

seat.title: Seat 14C
seat.text: 00:00. You’re alive. In your pocket there’s a wet boarding pass: 06:00, seat 14C.

ground.title: On the Ground
ground.text: 00:00. You’re alive. The planes keep passing over you, but you stay on the ground.
